intro: Ten criticisms were raised about the evidence behind ADA-FedAvg. This page says what this platform provides for each, and, just as importantly, what it cannot fix.

items.title: Statistical power: one seed, no confidence intervals, U2R has only 67 test rows
provides: Studies run each variant over 2–20 seeds; the seed changes both the data partition and the model initialisation.
Mean ± sd, 95% t-intervals and paired differences against FedAvg (matched by seed).
Per-class F1 shows how much of macro-F1 comes from the rare U2R class.
items.limits: Intervals are only as good as the seed count (use 10+). No multiple-comparison correction. U2R support is a property of KDDTest+, so read weighted metrics and per-class results next to macro-F1.

items.title: Is clustering the cause? Missing ablations
provides: Full-ablation preset: ADA with K = N (uniform client weights), random clusters of the same sizes, K = 2…8, and local class-weighted loss on/off. K = 1 is FedAvg.
items.limits: Pairing is by seed, so use the same seeds across variants (the presets do).

items.title: Missing baselines
provides: FedProx, IFCA (clustered FL) and FedAvg with a global class-balanced loss (weights = balanced^0.5 by default, adjustable).
items.limits: SCAFFOLD and CFL are not implemented. FedProx and IFCA are simplified: Adam local optimiser, and IFCA is scored with its best-by-validation cluster model, which is not how IFCA is normally evaluated. Astraea, FedLC and FedNova are not implemented.

items.title: The mechanism claim is unsupported
provides: Each experiment page shows per-class precision/recall/F1, the confusion matrix, false-alarm rate, attack-detection rate, cluster membership, cluster sizes and the true class mix of each cluster.
items.limits: A single run is an illustration, not evidence. Use a study before claiming a mechanism.

items.title: Does the clustering signal capture rare classes?
provides: The cluster class-mix table shows whether clusters track the benign/DoS ratio or rare-attack presence.
Alternative distances (log-scaled, inverse-frequency) can be compared in the ablation preset.
items.limits: Whether they help is an empirical question that the study answers. Do not assume it.

items.title: The centralized “upper bound” is not one
provides: Centralized runs use the same number of epochs as federated rounds (same sample passes), optionally with the same class-balanced loss, and appear in the Core comparison and Full ablation presets.
items.limits: The paper’s tuning of the centralized model is not recoverable. State its epochs, loss and optimiser.

items.title: Communication and privacy claims are inconsistent
provides: Results report summary bytes (the one-time histogram: clients × classes × 4).
Studies report rounds-to-target and mean ± sd convergence curves instead of an identical-by-construction byte count.
The Privacy page states exactly what is exchanged.
items.limits: Needs the authors. The abstract’s “without adding a single byte” and the title word “Privacy-Preserving” must change (for example “Privacy-Aware”), or differential privacy / secure aggregation must be added. This platform implements neither.

items.title: Robustness: a Sybil client can take a third of the global model
provides: Robustness preset: one simulated client flips labels and reports a fake histogram, comparing FedAvg, ADA and ADA with bounded cluster weights (blend: 0 = paper, 1 = FedAvg).
items.limits: A toy attack model with one attack type and no formal analysis.

items.title: Novelty, positioning and theory
items.limits: Needs the authors. Related-work positioning (Astraea, FedLC, FedNova, IFCA) and any theory, such as when equal cluster weights approximate a class-balanced objective, are not something software can supply. Verify every citation yourself.

items.title: Narrow experimental scope
provides: KDDTest-21, known-versus-novel attack detection (3,750 test records are attack types unseen in training), quantity skew, synthetic feature shift, up to 50 clients, and CSV upload with label mapping for other datasets.
items.limits: CIC-IDS2017 and FLNet2023 are not bundled; upload sampled CSVs and map their labels. The numpy trainer is slow beyond a few hundred thousand rows. Feature shift is simulated, not real organisational shift.

protocol: Run Core comparison and Full ablation at all three skew levels with at least 10 seeds.
Read the paired-difference table first: claim an effect only if the interval excludes 0 and the per-class table agrees.
Check ADA against random clusters and against FedAvg with class-balanced loss. If either matches ADA, the gain is reweighting, not clustering, and the paper should say so.
Report Test-21 and novel-attack results next to KDDTest+.
Export tables with the CSV / LaTeX buttons.
caveat: Single-seed development runs (30 rounds, moderate skew) gave FedAvg macro-F1 0.488 and ADA-FedAvg 0.468, against the paper’s 0.516 and 0.604. One seed each proves nothing either way; it is the reason to run studies before drawing conclusions.
